$comment: Beispiel-Universität building codes — INVENTED, for an invented institution, and that is the whole entry. Every other file of this kind in this folder records codes a real university publishes: OTH's come from its Standorte-und-Raumpläne page, TU Berlin's are surveyed into OpenStreetMap on the outlines themselves. This one has no such source and needs none.
$whyNotInherited: ⚠️ THE DEMO USED TO BORROW `tuberlin-building-letters.json` ALONG WITH THE BUILDINGS, AND IT GAVE THE GAME AWAY. Most codes are innocuous single letters, but the borrowed set also carried MAR, TIB, TIB17, HFT-FT, HFT-TA, EMH, BEL, KWT, TAP and TEM — and MAR is Marchstraße, TIB is the Technologie- und Innovationspark Berlin. Anyone who knows the reference campus reads those straight off a room list. Geometry can be borrowed without embarrassment; vocabulary cannot.
$whyUpperCase: ⚠️ UPPER CASE, WHICH LOOKS LIKE IT BREAKS THIS REPOSITORY'S RULE AND DOES NOT. The rule is that a lower-case code means the identifier is OURS rather than the university's — see `generate_timetable.py::building_rows` and the RWTH profile. Here there is no university distinct from us: the institution is invented, so its codes are its own by construction and there is no real identifier being usurped. Lower case would also make every room in the demo read as a placeholder, which is the opposite of what a demo is for.
source: generated by hand for config/aoi/campus-demo.json — no external source
$osmNameToLetterNote: Keyed by the OSM `name` of the shared buildings file, because that is what `generate_timetable.py::building_rows` looks up. The largest building is pinned to 'H' so that `rooms.heroBuilding` in the AOI resolves to the building the demo opens on.
